question: Which authority introduced new guidelines to enhance transparency in the coaching sector in November 2024?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**The Central Consumer Protection Authority**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA)** was established under the **Consumer Protection Act, 2019** to promote, protect, and enforce the rights of consumers.
 
• It is a **statutory body** formed to address issues related to unfair trade practices, misleading advertisements, and violation of consumer rights.
 
• The CCPA has the authority to investigate complaints, conduct inquiries, and take action against entities violating consumer laws.
 
• In **November 2024**, the CCPA introduced new guidelines focusing on transparency in the **coaching sector**, aiming to regulate practices and safeguard the interests of students.
 
• The guidelines may include provisions for **disclosure of fees**, refund policies, and ensuring ethical advertising practices.
 
• The authority works under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food, and Public Distribution** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Central Student Protection Authority**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect as no such authority exists under current Indian legislation or administrative frameworks.
 
 
 
• **The Central Costumer Protection Authority**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect due to the spelling error. The term "Costumer" refers to someone who designs costumes, and it does not relate to consumer protection.
 
 
 
• **The Central Vigilance Authority**__
 
 
• The **Central Vigilance Authority (CVC)** is a statutory body responsible for addressing corruption in government organizations.
 
• It was established under the **Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003**.
 
• The CVC deals with matters related to vigilance and does not oversee consumer protection or coaching sector regulations.
